questions.question: Which of the following best defines an amino acid?
options: An organic compound containing an amino group and a hydroxyl group.
An organic compound containing an amino group and a carboxyl group.
A polymer of peptides linked by glycosidic bonds.
A simple sugar molecule with an attached nitrogen atom.
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — An amino acid is defined by the presence of both an amino group (-NH2) and a carboxyl group (-COOH) attached to the same carbon (the alpha-carbon).

• Option A is incorrect because a hydroxyl group (-OH) is not the defining acidic group; amino acids contain a carboxyl group, not merely a hydroxyl group.
• Option C is incorrect because peptides are linked by peptide bonds, not glycosidic bonds; glycosidic bonds link sugars.
• Option D is incorrect because amino acids are not simple sugars with nitrogen; they are organic acids with an amino substituent.

questions.question: All amino acids found in proteins are alpha-amino acids. What does this signify?
options: The amino group is attached to the alpha-carbon, adjacent to the carboxyl group.
The amino group is on the terminal carbon of the side chain.
They all have the same stereochemistry (D-form).
They are all synthesized in the alpha-cells of the pancreas.
questions.explanation:
Correct: A — In an alpha-amino acid, the amino group is attached to the alpha-carbon, which is the carbon immediately adjacent to the carboxyl carbon.

• Option B is incorrect because the amino group is not on the terminal side-chain carbon; it is on the alpha-carbon.
• Option C is incorrect because naturally occurring protein amino acids are predominantly L-enantiomers, not D-forms.
• Option D is incorrect because alpha-amino acids are not synthesized in pancreatic alpha-cells; that phrase confuses the alpha-carbon with pancreatic cell types.

questions.question: Based on the number of amino and carboxyl groups, into which category does Glutamic acid fall?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Glutamic acid has two carboxyl groups and one amino group, giving it a net acidic character; it is therefore classified as an acidic amino acid.

• Option A is incorrect because neutral amino acids have equal numbers of amino and carboxyl groups.
• Option B is incorrect because basic amino acids have more amino/basic groups than carboxyl groups.
• Option D is incorrect because aromatic amino acids are classified by an aromatic side chain, not by acidic group count.

questions.question: Which of the following is a basic amino acid?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Lysine contains an extra amino group in its side chain, making it a basic amino acid with a positive charge at physiological pH.

• Option A is incorrect because aspartic acid is an acidic amino acid.
• Option B is incorrect because alanine is a neutral, non-polar amino acid.
• Option D is incorrect because valine is a neutral, non-polar branched-chain amino acid.

questions.question: Phenylalanine, Tyrosine, and Tryptophan are classified as:
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan all contain aromatic rings in their side chains, so they are classified as aromatic amino acids.

• Option A is incorrect because aliphatic amino acids have non-aromatic hydrocarbon side chains.
• Option C is incorrect because sulphur-containing amino acids include cysteine and methionine.
• Option D is incorrect because although tryptophan contains a heterocyclic indole ring, the group as a whole is classified as aromatic; heterocyclic is not the standard class for all three.

questions.question: Which of the following is an imino acid?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Proline is called an imino acid because its side chain forms a cyclic structure with the amino group, giving it a secondary amine (imino) character.

• Option A is incorrect because glycine is the simplest amino acid with a primary amino group.
• Option C is incorrect because serine is a hydroxyl-containing amino acid.
• Option D is incorrect because arginine is a basic amino acid with a guanidino group.

questions.question: Which of these is a sulphur-containing amino acid?
questions.explanation:
Correct: D — Cysteine contains a thiol (-SH) group in its side chain and is a sulphur-containing amino acid.

• Option A is incorrect because serine contains a hydroxyl group, not sulphur.
• Option B is incorrect because threonine contains a hydroxyl group, not sulphur.
• Option C is incorrect because tyrosine contains a phenol group, not sulphur.

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as an essential amino acid?
questions.explanation:
Correct: D — Methionine is an essential amino acid; it cannot be synthesized by the human body and must be obtained from the diet.

• Option A is incorrect because alanine is non-essential.
• Option B is incorrect because aspartic acid is non-essential.
• Option C is incorrect because glutamic acid is non-essential.

questions.question: Which of these amino acids is considered non-essential in human nutrition?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Tyrosine is considered non-essential because it can be synthesized in the body from phenylalanine.

• Option A is incorrect because leucine is an essential amino acid.
• Option B is incorrect because valine is an essential amino acid.
• Option D is incorrect because tryptophan is an essential amino acid.

questions.question: An amino acid that can be converted to glucose is termed:
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — A glucogenic amino acid is one whose carbon skeleton can be converted into glucose via gluconeogenesis.

• Option A is incorrect because ketogenic amino acids are converted to ketone bodies, not glucose.
• Option C is incorrect because essential refers to dietary requirement, not metabolic fate.
• Option D is incorrect because non-polar refers to side-chain chemistry, not glucose formation.

questions.question: Which of the following is a purely ketogenic amino acid?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Leucine is a purely ketogenic amino acid; its carbon skeleton is converted only to ketone bodies, not to glucose.

• Option A is incorrect because isoleucine is both glucogenic and ketogenic.
• Option B is incorrect because phenylalanine is both glucogenic and ketogenic.
• Option D is incorrect because tyrosine is both glucogenic and ketogenic.

questions.question: Amino acids that are both glucogenic and ketogenic include:
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Isoleucine and phenylalanine are examples of amino acids that can be converted to both glucose and ketone bodies.

• Option A is incorrect because leucine and lysine are purely ketogenic.
• Option B is incorrect because alanine and glycine are glucogenic only.
• Option D is incorrect because valine and methionine are glucogenic, not both glucogenic and ketogenic.

questions.question: According to side chain polarity, Valine is classified as a:
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Valine has a branched hydrocarbon side chain, making it hydrophobic and non-polar.

• Option A is incorrect because hydrophilic polar amino acids have polar side chains such as -OH or -NH2.
• Option C is incorrect because positively charged amino acids include lysine and arginine.
• Option D is incorrect because negatively charged amino acids include aspartate and glutamate.

questions.question: Which of the following amino acids is hydrophilic and uncharged polar at physiological pH?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Serine has a hydroxyl (-OH) side chain, making it hydrophilic and uncharged polar at physiological pH.

• Option A is incorrect because leucine is hydrophobic and non-polar.
• Option B is incorrect because methionine is hydrophobic and non-polar.
• Option D is incorrect because lysine is positively charged at physiological pH.

questions.question: Which two amino acids are negatively charged at physiological pH?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Aspartic acid and glutamic acid have acidic side chains that lose protons at physiological pH, giving them a net negative charge.

• Option A is incorrect because lysine and arginine are positively charged.
• Option C is incorrect because serine and threonine are uncharged polar amino acids.
• Option D is incorrect because histidine and lysine are positively charged or partially positive, not negatively charged.

questions.question: What is the primary reason most amino acids are optically active?
options: They contain an asymmetric alpha-carbon atom.
They are all found in the L-configuration.
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Most amino acids have four different groups attached to the alpha-carbon, making it asymmetric (chiral) and therefore optically active.

• Option A is incorrect because a carboxyl group alone does not create optical activity.
• Option C is incorrect because being in the L-configuration is a consequence of chirality, not the primary reason for optical activity.
• Option D is incorrect because zwitterion formation does not explain optical activity.

questions.question: Which amino acid is the exception to the rule that all amino acids are optically active?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Glycine has two hydrogen atoms on its alpha-carbon, so it lacks a chiral center and is not optically active.

• Option A is incorrect because alanine has a chiral alpha-carbon.
• Option B is incorrect because proline has a chiral alpha-carbon.
• Option D is incorrect because cysteine has a chiral alpha-carbon.

questions.question: The property of amino acids to react with both acids and bases is known as:
questions.explanation:
Correct: A — Amphoterism is the ability of a molecule to act as both an acid and a base; amino acids are amphoteric because they contain both acidic and basic groups.

• Option B is incorrect because denaturation refers to loss of protein structure.
• Option C is incorrect because isoelectric focusing is a separation technique based on isoelectric point.
• Option D is incorrect because decarboxylation is the removal of a carboxyl group as CO2.

questions.question: The pH at which an amino acid carries no net electrical charge is called its:
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — The isoelectric point (IEP) is the pH at which the amino acid has no net charge and exists mainly as a zwitterion.

• Option A is incorrect because pKa is the pH at which a specific ionizable group is half-dissociated.
• Option B is incorrect because optimum pH usually refers to enzyme activity.
• Option D is incorrect because neutral point is not the standard biochemical term for this concept.

questions.question: At a pH below its isoelectric point, an amino acid will exist primarily as a:
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Below the isoelectric point, the medium is more acidic, so the amino acid is protonated and carries a net positive charge (cation).

• Option A is incorrect because the zwitterion predominates at the isoelectric point.
• Option C is incorrect because the anion predominates above the isoelectric point.
• Option D is incorrect because the molecule is charged, not neutral, away from the IEP.

questions.question: What is the form of an amino acid at its isoelectric point called?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — At the isoelectric point, the amino acid exists predominantly as a zwitterion, containing both positive and negative charges with a net charge of zero.

• Option A is incorrect because the anion form dominates at pH above the IEP.
• Option B is incorrect because the cation form dominates at pH below the IEP.
• Option D is incorrect because radical ions are not the standard form of amino acids at the IEP.

questions.question: Why do amino acids precipitate most readily at their isoelectric point?
options: The molecules have no net charge and repel each other less.
They form covalent bonds with each other.
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — At the isoelectric point, amino acid molecules have no net charge, so electrostatic repulsion between them is minimized, allowing them to aggregate and precipitate.

• Option A is incorrect because denaturation applies to proteins, not simple amino acids.
• Option C is incorrect because precipitation at the IEP does not involve new covalent bonds.
• Option D is incorrect because solubility is lowest, not highest, at the isoelectric point.

questions.question: Which reagent reacts with the amino group of most amino acids to liberate nitrogen gas, but not with proline?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Nitrous acid reacts with primary amino groups to release nitrogen gas; proline has a secondary amino group and does not give this reaction.

• Option A is incorrect because ninhydrin produces a colour change, not nitrogen gas.
• Option C is incorrect because acetyl chloride acetylates amino groups.
• Option D is incorrect because methyl iodide methylates amino groups.

questions.question: The reaction of an amino acid with an alcohol forms:
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — The carboxyl group of an amino acid reacts with an alcohol to form an ester, often in the presence of an acid catalyst.

• Option A is incorrect because salt formation occurs with acids or bases, not alcohols.
• Option C is incorrect because amide formation involves reaction with an amine.
• Option D is incorrect because peptide formation involves reaction with another amino acid.

questions.question: The decarboxylation of histidine produces which physiologically active compound?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Decarboxylation of histidine removes CO2 and produces histamine, a mediator of allergic and inflammatory responses.

• Option A is incorrect because tryptamine is derived from tryptophan.
• Option B is incorrect because ethanolamine is derived from serine.
• Option D is incorrect because serotonin is derived from tryptophan.

questions.question: The reaction of an amino acid with acetyl chloride is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Acetyl chloride reacts with the amino group of an amino acid to add an acetyl group, so the reaction is acetylation.

• Option A is incorrect because decarboxylation removes CO2.
• Option C is incorrect because methylation uses methyl iodide or similar reagents.
• Option D is incorrect because deamination removes an amino group.

questions.question: Oxidative deamination of an amino acid produces:
options: A hydroxyl fatty acid and NH3
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Oxidative deamination removes the amino group as ammonia and converts the carbon skeleton to an alpha-keto acid.

• Option A is incorrect because a fatty acid is not the direct product of amino acid oxidative deamination.
• Option B is incorrect because a hydroxyl fatty acid is not the product.
• Option D is incorrect because the amino group is removed as NH3, not left as a primary amine, and CO2 is not the direct product.

questions.question: The formation of a peptide bond is a reaction between:
options: The R-groups of two amino acids.
The amino group of one amino acid and the carboxyl group of another.
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — A peptide bond forms by condensation between the alpha-amino group of one amino acid and the alpha-carboxyl group of another, with loss of water.

• Option A is incorrect because R-groups are not directly involved in the peptide backbone bond.
• Option C is incorrect because carboxyl-carboxyl reaction does not form a peptide bond.
• Option D is incorrect because amino-amino reaction does not form a peptide bond.

questions.question: Which colour is produced when most amino acids react with Ninhydrin?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Most amino acids react with ninhydrin to produce a blue or blue-purple colour (often called Ruhemann's purple). The key marks blue as the expected answer.

• Option A is incorrect because yellow is typical of proline, not most amino acids.
• Option C is incorrect because red is not the standard ninhydrin colour.
• Option D is incorrect because although purple is often used to describe the complex, the option marked correct in the key is blue.

questions.question: Which amino acid gives a yellow colour with Ninhydrin?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Proline contains a secondary amine and reacts with ninhydrin to give a yellow colour rather than the usual blue-purple.

• Option A is incorrect because glycine gives the typical blue-purple colour.
• Option B is incorrect because tryptophan gives a blue-purple colour.
• Option D is incorrect because tyrosine gives a blue-purple colour.

questions.question: The Xanthoproteic test is used to detect the presence of which type of amino acids?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — The xanthoproteic test involves nitration of aromatic rings, so it detects aromatic amino acids such as phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan.

• Option A is incorrect because sulphur-containing amino acids are detected by other tests such as the lead acetate test.
• Option C is incorrect because basic amino acids are not the target of the xanthoproteic test.
• Option D is incorrect because acidic amino acids are not specifically detected by this test.

questions.question: Millon's test is specific for which amino acid due to its phenol group?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Millon's reagent reacts with the phenol group of tyrosine to give a red colour, making the test relatively specific for tyrosine.

• Option A is incorrect because tryptophan contains an indole ring, not a phenol group.
• Option B is incorrect because phenylalanine lacks a phenol group.
• Option D is incorrect because histidine contains an imidazole group, not a phenol group.

questions.question: The Rosenheim test is a specific test for which amino acid?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — The Rosenheim test is used to detect tryptophan, often based on its indole ring reactivity.

• Option A is incorrect because cysteine is detected by sulphur-specific tests.
• Option B is incorrect because proline is detected by ninhydrin yellow colour or other tests.
• Option D is incorrect because arginine is detected by tests such as the Sakaguchi test.

questions.question: Which of the following elements is a defining component of proteins, constituting about 16% of their mass?
questions.explanation:
Correct: D — Proteins are characterized by a high nitrogen content, averaging about 16% of their mass, which is used in the Kjeldahl method to estimate protein content.

• Option A is incorrect because carbon is abundant in all organic molecules, not defining for proteins.
• Option B is incorrect because hydrogen is not the defining element of proteins.
• Option C is incorrect because oxygen is also common in carbohydrates and lipids.

questions.question: Proteins are polymers of amino acids linked by which type of bond?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Amino acids in proteins are joined by peptide bonds, which are amide linkages formed by condensation.

• Option A is incorrect because glycosidic bonds link sugars in carbohydrates.
• Option C is incorrect because ester bonds are found in lipids and some other molecules.
• Option D is incorrect because hydrogen bonds are non-covalent interactions that stabilize protein structure, not the primary backbone linkage.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a biological function of proteins?
options: Providing structural support in skin and bone.
Transporting lipids and hormones in the blood.
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Storing genetic information is the function of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), not proteins.

• Option A is incorrect because enzymes are proteins and catalyze metabolic reactions.
• Option C is incorrect because structural proteins such as collagen provide support in skin and bone.
• Option D is incorrect because transport proteins such as albumin carry lipids and hormones in blood.

questions.question: The colloidal nature of proteins is demonstrated by which two phenomena?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Proteins are colloids; their colloidal nature is shown by the Tyndall effect (scattering of light) and Brownian movement (random motion of particles).

• Option A is incorrect because osmosis and diffusion are general properties of solutions, not specific demonstrations of colloids.
• Option B is incorrect because dialysis and precipitation are separation techniques, not direct demonstrations of colloidal nature.
• Option D is incorrect because hydrolysis and denaturation are chemical changes, not colloidal properties.

questions.question: Why are proteins considered non-dialyzable?
options: They are too large to pass through a semipermeable membrane.
They precipitate at their isoelectric point.
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Proteins are large macromolecules and cannot pass through the pores of a semipermeable dialysis membrane, so they are retained while small molecules diffuse out.

• Option A is incorrect because charge is not the main reason; size is.
• Option C is incorrect because many proteins are soluble in water.
• Option D is incorrect because precipitation at the IEP is not the reason for non-dialyzability.

questions.question: The ability of proteins to act as buffers is due to their:
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Proteins contain both acidic and basic groups and can donate or accept protons, so their amphoteric nature allows them to act as buffers.

• Option A is incorrect because high molecular weight does not directly explain buffering.
• Option B is incorrect because colloidal nature relates to particle size, not proton exchange.
• Option D is incorrect because peptide bonds are not the main buffering groups.

questions.question: The process of denaturation of a protein involves:
options: The complete hydrolysis of the protein into amino acids.
The destruction of secondary and tertiary structures without breaking peptide bonds.
The synthesis of new peptide bonds.
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Denaturation disrupts the non-covalent interactions that maintain secondary, tertiary, and quaternary structure, but the primary sequence and peptide bonds remain intact.

• Option A is incorrect because breaking peptide bonds is hydrolysis, not denaturation.
• Option B is incorrect because complete hydrolysis to amino acids is a more extensive process.
• Option D is incorrect because denaturation does not synthesize new peptide bonds.

questions.question: Which of the following is a physical denaturing agent for proteins?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — High temperature is a physical agent that disrupts non-covalent interactions and denatures proteins.

• Option A is incorrect because strong acid is a chemical denaturing agent.
• Option B is incorrect because heavy metals are chemical denaturants.
• Option D is incorrect because organic solvents are chemical denaturants.

questions.question: Which of the following is a key characteristic of a denatured protein?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Denaturation usually destroys the native conformation and therefore leads to loss of biological activity.

• Option A is incorrect because denatured proteins often become less soluble and may precipitate.
• Option C is incorrect because enzymatic function is typically lost, not enhanced.
• Option D is incorrect because the denatured state is usually less ordered and less stable functionally.

questions.question: What is the net charge of an amino acid at a pH well above its isoelectric point?
options: It depends on the amino acid.
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — At a pH above the isoelectric point, the amino acid is deprotonated and carries a net negative charge.

• Option A is incorrect because a positive charge occurs at pH below the IEP.
• Option C is incorrect because zero net charge occurs at the IEP.
• Option D is incorrect because the general rule applies to amino acids with ionizable groups.

questions.question: Which amino acid is a precursor for the synthesis of serotonin and melatonin?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Tryptophan is the precursor for serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine) and melatonin.

• Option A is incorrect because tyrosine is a precursor for catecholamines and thyroid hormones.
• Option B is incorrect because histidine is a precursor for histamine.
• Option D is incorrect because phenylalanine is converted to tyrosine, not directly to serotonin.

questions.question: Which of the following amino acids does NOT contain a chiral center?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Glycine has two hydrogen atoms attached to its alpha-carbon, so it is achiral.

• Option A is incorrect because alanine has a chiral alpha-carbon.
• Option C is incorrect because threonine has two chiral centers.
• Option D is incorrect because leucine has a chiral alpha-carbon.

questions.question: The unique feature of proline is that its side chain forms a cyclic structure with its:
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Proline is unique because its side chain cyclizes with the amino group, forming a secondary amine (imino acid).

• Option A is incorrect because the side chain does not cyclize with the carboxyl group.
• Option C is incorrect because the alpha-carbon is part of the ring but the key feature is the amino group involvement.
• Option D is incorrect because the side chain does not cyclize with a hydrogen atom.

questions.question: The covalent bond that links the sulfur atoms of two cysteine molecules is called a:
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Two cysteine residues can be oxidized to form a covalent disulfide bond (-S-S-) between their thiol groups.

• Option A is incorrect because peptide bonds link amino acids through the backbone.
• Option B is incorrect because hydrogen bonds are non-covalent.
• Option D is incorrect because ionic bonds are electrostatic interactions between charged groups.

questions.question: In the reaction Amino Acid + CO2 -> Carbamino compound, which group is involved?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Carbon dioxide reacts with the amino group of an amino acid to form a carbamino compound, as occurs with hemoglobin.

• Option A is incorrect because the carboxyl group is not the site of carbamino formation.
• Option B is incorrect because R-groups are not generally involved in carbamino formation.
• Option D is incorrect because the alpha-carbon is not the reactive site.

questions.question: Which of these plasma proteins is responsible for carrying hormones, minerals, and lipids?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Albumin is the most abundant plasma protein and serves as a carrier for hormones, minerals, lipids, and drugs.

• Option A is incorrect because antibodies are involved in immune defense.
• Option B is incorrect because hemoglobin transports oxygen.
• Option D is incorrect because collagen is a structural protein, not a plasma carrier.

questions.question: Which of the following is an essential amino acid that is also a precursor to histamine?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Histidine is an essential amino acid and is decarboxylated to form histamine.

• Option A is incorrect because lysine is essential but not the precursor to histamine.
• Option B is incorrect because arginine is conditionally essential and not the direct precursor to histamine.
• Option D is incorrect because methionine is essential but not the precursor to histamine.

questions.question: The isoelectric point (IEP) is crucial for protein separation techniques because at this pH, proteins:
options: Have maximum charge and mobility in an electric field.
Are most easily precipitated and have zero mobility.
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — At the IEP, a protein has no net charge, so it does not migrate in an electric field and is most easily precipitated.

• Option A is incorrect because solubility is usually minimal at the IEP.
• Option B is incorrect because maximum charge and mobility occur away from the IEP.
• Option D is incorrect because solubility in organic solvents is not the basis of IEP separation.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs are both basic amino acids with a net positive charge at physiological pH?
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Lysine and arginine have basic side chains that are protonated and positively charged at physiological pH.

• Option A is incorrect because aspartate and glutamate are acidic and negatively charged.
• Option C is incorrect because serine and threonine are uncharged polar amino acids.
• Option D is incorrect because leucine and isoleucine are non-polar amino acids.

questions.question: What type of reaction produces a peptide bond?
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — A peptide bond is formed by a condensation (dehydration synthesis) reaction between an amino group and a carboxyl group, with loss of water.

• Option A is incorrect because hydrolysis breaks peptide bonds.
• Option B is incorrect because oxidation is not the primary reaction in peptide bond formation.
• Option D is incorrect because deamination removes amino groups.

questions.question: The alpha-helix and beta-pleated sheet are examples of a protein's:
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Alpha-helices and beta-pleated sheets are regular local folding patterns that constitute secondary structure.

• Option A is incorrect because primary structure is the amino acid sequence.
• Option C is incorrect because tertiary structure is the overall 3D folding of a single polypeptide.
• Option D is incorrect because quaternary structure involves multiple polypeptide subunits.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a denaturing agent?
options: A gentle increase in temperature to optimal physiological level.
questions.explanation:
Correct: D — A gentle increase to the optimal physiological temperature supports normal protein function and is not a denaturing condition.

• Option A is incorrect because urea disrupts hydrogen bonding and denatures proteins.
• Option B is incorrect because X-rays can damage proteins and cause denaturation.
• Option C is incorrect because detergents disrupt hydrophobic interactions and denature proteins.

questions.question: The reaction of an amino acid with methyl iodide is called:
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Methyl iodide adds a methyl group to the amino group, so the reaction is methylation.

• Option A is incorrect because acetylation uses acetyl chloride or acetic anhydride.
• Option C is incorrect because deamination removes an amino group.
• Option D is incorrect because decarboxylation removes CO2.

questions.question: The conversion of Serine to Ethanolamine is an example of:
questions.explanation:
Correct: C — Serine is decarboxylated to ethanolamine, a reaction that removes the carboxyl group as CO2.

• Option A is incorrect because transamination transfers an amino group to a keto acid.
• Option B is incorrect because oxidative deamination removes an amino group as ammonia.
• Option D is incorrect because hydrolysis breaks bonds using water.

questions.question: What is a zwitterion?
options: An ion with two positive charges.
A molecule with both positive and negative charges but a net charge of zero.
An ion with two negative charges.
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — A zwitterion has both positive and negative charges within the same molecule but carries no net charge overall.

• Option A is incorrect because a zwitterion is not defined by two positive charges.
• Option C is incorrect because a zwitterion is not defined by two negative charges.
• Option D is incorrect because a zwitterion is a charge state, not a size class of protein.

questions.question: Proteins are crucial for the immune system because they form:
questions.explanation:
Correct: B — Antibodies are immunoglobulins, which are proteins produced by the immune system to recognize and neutralize antigens.

• Option A is incorrect because antigens are substances that trigger an immune response, not the proteins that defend the body.
• Option C is incorrect because buffers help maintain pH, not specifically immune defense.
• Option D is incorrect because hormones are signaling molecules, not the main immune proteins.

questions.question: The peptide linkage in a protein is represented as:
questions.explanation:
Correct: A — The peptide bond is an amide linkage represented as -CO-NH- between the carbonyl carbon of one amino acid and the amino nitrogen of the next.

• Option B is incorrect because -CO-O- represents an ester linkage.
• Option C is incorrect because it is the same amide linkage written in reverse order, but the standard representation is -CO-NH-.
• Option D is incorrect because -NH-NH- is not a peptide bond.
